newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Shining Path rebels plant explosives in Lima.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Shining Path rebels plant explosives in Lima.

text.p: Maoist Shining Path guerrillas draped a red hammer-and-sickle flag over a footbridge in downtown Lima on Monday and laid some small explosives nearby, Peruvian police said.
"From the symbols and the explosives planted to avoid the withdrawal of the flag, we know it is Shining Path," said a spokesman for the police anti-explosives unit (UDEX).
Police defused the explosives and took down the flag.
The spokesman said the action was part of a campaign to mark the anniversary of the day Shining Path took up of arms against the Peruvian state on May 17, 1980.
The group also exploded a powerful car-bomb at a police station in Lima last week, injuring at least eight officers and causing widespread damage.
Violence unleashed by Shining Path and the smaller Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) has cost 30,000 lives and $25 billion in infrastructure damage in Peru since 1980.
Fourteen MRTA guerrillas died last month in the Japanese ambassador's house where they held 72 hostages for four months until the diplomatic residence was stormed by Peruvian troops.
